region.text: the Sanjak of Scutari, now a semi-autonomous pashalik; with Bar and Podgorica, which the Sanjak of Scutari page lists as its towns

ledger.note: 1757: Mehmed Bushati, "having eliminated two rival families", proclaims himself pasha of Shkodër and transforms "the Sanjak of Scutari, created in 1479, into a semi-autonomous Pashalik of Shkodra". The page gives the sanjak, not its boundary. Bar and Podgorica added from the Sanjak of Scutari page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjak_of_Scutari): "ownership of the cities of Bar, Podgorica, Spuž and Ulcinj was transferred from the Sanjak of Scutari" in 1876-78. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: Bar and Podgorica added to the found region]

region.text: Ulcinj, "captured the city" in 1772 while Mahmud served his father

ledger.note: 1772: Mahmud captures Ulcinj. The page does not say from whom, so the counterpart is the Porte's authority in the sanjak.

region.text: Durrës, taken "in June 1780"; the Kavaja and Kruja raids are undated

ledger.note: 1780: Kara Mahmud takes Durrës ("In June 1780 ... eventually took possession of Durrës"). The page does not name the previous holder. The page dates the tax-farming quarrel to June 1780 and says only that he "eventually took possession of Durrës": month dropped, confidence 2 [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01].

region.text: Montenegro: Kara Mahmud "conquered it in just four days" in 1785

ledger.note: 1785: Kara Mahmud attacks and defeats Montenegro. The Pashalik page counts southern Montenegro as pashalik land to 1830; the Kara Mahmud page shows Montenegro still fighting in 1796, so the zone is contested, not annexed.

region.text: Venetian Albania and the Bay of Kotor: Kara Mahmud "forced the Venetians to pay him a tribute (haraç)"

ledger.note: 1785: Venice pays haraç to the pasha. The Kara Mahmud page dates the conflict with Venice to 1785; neither page dates the tribute's end, so the end is a bridge to the fall of the Republic in 1797 recorded at confidence 1.
1795: "he conquered parts of Southern Albania and much of Kosovo". Kosovo had been under the Ottoman sanjaks and local beys; the page names no state.

region.text: the Dibra, Debar and Tetovo marches of western Macedonia, part of the peak extent

ledger.note: Page silent on the date: the Pashalik page says the peak held "western Macedonia" and the 1831 demand names Debar, Ohrid, Elbasan and Trgovište. Year bridged to the 1795 Kosovo campaign.

region.text: Montenegro, after the Battle of Krusi

ledger.note: 1796: "Kara Mahmud was killed and decapitated in battle" at Krusi on 22 September after losing at Martinići in July; the Montenegrin tribes keep their mountains.

region.text: the Bjelopavlići (Danilovgrad) and the Piperi, who joined Montenegro after the victory of 1796

ledger.note: 22 September 1796: Kara Mahmud "was killed and decapitated in battle" at Krusi; the Montenegrin victory brought the Bjelopavlići and Piperi into Montenegro (Prince-Bishopric infobox: "Unification of (old) Montenegro and the Hills (1796)"). Same region as the gain in prince-bishopric-of-montenegro. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added]

region.text: Venetian Albania and Kotor, until the Republic ended

ledger.note: 1796: Kara Mahmud dies; the tribute is not mentioned again by the pages opened. Bridging year, confidence 1.

region.text: "the sanjak of Berat was appropriated to him" in 1820

ledger.note: 1820: Berat goes to Mustafa. The Mustafa page does not say from whom; the Yanina page has Ali Pasha invading Berat in 1809 and declared a rebel in 1820, so Ali's Pashalik of Yanina is the counterpart by the researcher's reading.

region.text: "the sanjaks of Ohrid and Elbasan were appropriated to him" in 1824

ledger.note: 1824: Ohrid and Elbasan come to the Bushatis after Ali Pasha of Yanina's fall (he died in January 1822).

region.text: Macedonia: the Porte "demanded he hand over Dukakin, Debar, Elbasan, Ohrid and Trgovište"; "Mid-March 1831: he led an army against Grand Vizier Reşid Mehmed Pasha"

ledger.note: March 1831: the pasha rebels against Mahmud II and marches into Macedonia; routed at Skopje in early May.

region.text: Macedonia and the siege of Scutari

ledger.note: 10 November 1831: Mustafa Pasha Bushati surrenders in Scutari after a six-month siege.

1831: "Mehmed Reshid Pasha besieged Rozafa castle and forced the surrender of the last pasha Mustafa Bushati"; the pashalik is dissolved and its land returns to the sanjak and the Monastir Eyalet. The region is the keyframe of 1824-1831 (fifteen districts: Shkodër, Lezhë, Kukës, Ulcinj, Durrës, Tiranë, Dibër, Bar, Podgorica, Kosovo, Debar, Tetovo, Berat, Elbasan, Ohrid) without the Montenegrin land of 1796. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: region widened to the whole pashalik]

wars.name: Kara Mahmud Bushati's campaigns against Montenegro
wars.outcome: Kara Mahmud defeated Montenegro in 1785 in four days; in 1796 he lost at Martinići (July) and was killed at the Battle of Krusi (22 September 1796). Montenegro kept its mountains.
wars.note: The Pashalik page counts southern Montenegro as pashalik land to 1830.

wars.name: Revolt of Mustafa Pasha Bushati against Mahmud II
wars.outcome: The Porte demanded Dukakin, Debar, Elbasan, Ohrid and Trgovište; Mustafa was routed at Skopje in early May 1831 and surrendered Scutari on 10 November 1831. The pashalik ended.

certainty.note: A de facto autonomous pashalik with no treaty frontier; the extent of every period rests on the places named in the pages, and the Pashalik page's peak extent (southeastern Serbia, most of Montenegro) is wider than anything dated.

notes: Cliopatria has no row; all five keyframes are new. Peak extent (Pashalik page) is wider than the dated gains: southeastern Serbia and "most of Montenegro" are undated and left out of the keyframes; they are unverified. Disagreements: the Kara Mahmud page says he conquered "most of the Pashalik of Berat" without a date, while the Yanina page has Ali Pasha invading Berat in 1809 and the Mustafa page has the sanjak "appropriated" to Mustafa in 1820; Elbasan is claimed for Kara Mahmud (undated) and given to Mustafa in 1824. The 1785 Venetian tribute is from the Pashalik page and has no dated end (confidence-1 bridge to 1796). Counterparts needing dossiers: pashalik-of-berat (Berat sanjak), prince-bishopric-of-montenegro (written in this batch), pashalik-of-yanina (written in this batch). Wikidata id left null (wikidata.org unreachable). Review fix (2026-11-01): (1) The 1796 loss to Montenegro now exists (same region as prince-bishopric-of-montenegro ledger 4: Danilovgrad municipality and the 25 km circle round 19.1 E, 42.65 N) and the keyframes of 1796-1831 subtract it, so the 3-cell overlap with Montenegro is gone; the keyframe of 1795 is split off. (2) Bar and Podgorica are in the found region and the keyframes from 1757, on the strength of the Sanjak of Scutari page (they were towns of the sanjak until 1876-78), instead of entering unexplained in 1795; Ulcinj stays a 1772 gain and the first keyframe is split at 1772. (3) The dissolve region and the successor land are the 1824-1831 union (fifteen districts) without the Montenegrin land. (4) The month of the Durrës event was removed and its confidence lowered to 2 by the reviewer; I agree (the Kara Mahmud page says only that he "eventually took possession of Durrës"). Still thin: the Venetian haraç (1785-1796 bridge, confidence 1), the date of the Dibra-Debar-Tetovo march (confidence 1), and southeastern Serbia and "most of Montenegro" (undated, not drawn); the pages opened give no more. The Cetinje circle of prince-bishopric-of-montenegro is subtracted from every keyframe (one Podgorica cell); one Bar/Budva cell (42.26 N, 19.09 E) is still shared with Montenegro in 1813-1814, when Montenegro's keyframe adds Budva (its own note says the page is silent on whether Montenegro held Budva).
